title_en: Japan proposes extending Noto earthquake employment-secondment support while tightening subsidy conditions

quick_take.what_changed: On 2 November 2026, MHLW opened consultation on extending the Noto earthquake employment-stability subsidy for secondments from up to two years to up to three years, subject to a 31 December 2027 subsidy end date.
quick_take.who_is_affected: Originating employers whose operations were curtailed for economic reasons linked to the 2024 Noto Peninsula earthquake, receiving employers and seconded workers, subject to the scheme's formal eligibility conditions.
quick_take.what_to_do_now: Review the draft and submit comments by 1 December 2026; distinguish the proposed extension and reduced subsidy rates from rules currently in force.

paragraphs: The 2024 Noto Peninsula earthquake reduced business activity and disrupted local employment. Japan's existing disaster employment-stability scheme supports secondments that keep employees attached to the originating employer while another business temporarily accepts their labour. This makes retention possible without assuming that the original workplace can immediately resume normal operations.

Under the current scheme, eligible secondments last one month to two years and contracts must fall within the existing scheme period ending on 31 December 2026. MHLW specifically cites conditions in the jurisdictions of the Nanao and Wajima public employment security offices in explaining the extension; this reference alone does not establish that the scheme is restricted to those two jurisdictions. Extending time support while asking originating employers for a reopening plan aims to distinguish temporary disaster recovery from indefinite wage support.

MHLW established the disaster-specific incentive on 17 December 2024. The official consultation outline records existing subsidy rates of 4/5 for small and medium-sized enterprises and 2/3 for other businesses, subject to an upper limit of 9,110 yen per person per day. These are descriptions of the current scheme, not new obligations.

On 2 November 2026, MHLW published a proposal under Article 62(2) of the Employment Insurance Act (Act No. 116 of 1974; Showa 49), with public comments accepted through 1 December 2026. The proposal would extend eligible secondment duration to three years while limiting subsidised time to 31 December 2027, add a workplace-reopening plan condition, and lower rates for originating employers first filing a secondment plan on or after 1 January 2027.

confirmed.text: The draft was released for consultation on 2 November 2026, with comments due on 1 December 2026.

expected: MHLW's consultation outline envisages promulgation in late December 2026 and commencement on promulgation; neither is a confirmed legal event as of verification.
uncertainties: Final provisions, any changes following consultation, and actual promulgation and commencement must be checked against the issued ordinance. The proposed lower rates must not be presented as already binding.

paragraphs: For affected originating employers, the proposed extension may preserve a route to retention while recovery continues. The additional reopening-plan condition would require clearer evidence of an intended return to operations; that condition remains a proposal pending enactment.

For employers submitting their first secondment plan on or after 1 January 2027, the draft would lower the incentive rate from 4/5 to 2/3 for SMEs and from 2/3 to 1/2 for other businesses. Employers should not apply the proposed rates prematurely and should check the relevant plan submission date and official eligibility criteria.
checklist: Check the originating employer's eligibility under the official Noto disaster scheme, including the earthquake-related economic impact, and document the intended resumption of business.
Compare existing and proposed secondment periods, application timing and subsidy rates; consult the public-comment materials before 1 December 2026.

review_notes: Checked against the e-Gov consultation case 495260245 and the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare one-page official proposal outline on 2026-11-05. Consultation is open until 2026-12-01. The existing Employment Insurance Act Enforcement Regulation is Showa 50 Labour Ministry Ordinance No. 3; a proposed amendment has no promulgated ordinance number. Existing subsidy terms, proposed extension, 2027 cutoff, plan requirement and reduced subsidy rates are distinguished from binding current rules. Nanao/Wajima jurisdiction references explain MHLW policy rationale but do not prove geographic exclusivity. The unrelated October 2026 Kumamoto special measure is not part of this proposal. English, Japanese and Chinese sections reviewed individually for matching claims, dates, legal thresholds and pending status.
